summary: actor-core owns the SWSEV2BaseActor document class, the two-phase derived pipeline (sync per-type compute in prepareDerivedData plus async DerivedCalculator.computeAll, coalesced by signature and stamped by derived-generation), and the ActorEngine mutation gate. ActorEngine is the de-facto single write path but exposes five plan grammars, orchestrates combat/force resource rules, and sits inside an 18-file static import cycle with the derived calculators. No live critical defects found; the non-atomic cross-actor move has no live caller.

findings.title: 18-file static import cycle between derived calculators, combat-roll-math/combat-stat-rules, ModifierEngine and ActorEngine
findings.observed: Four loops close the SCC: (1) level-split -> utils/hardening (for warnIfMixedTracks) -> ActorEngine -> DerivedCalculator -> level-split; (2) ModifierEngine -> WeaponsEngine -> combat-roll-math -> ModifierEngine; (3) combat-roll-math -> RageEngine -> ActorEngine -> DerivedCalculator -> ModifierEngine -> WeaponsEngine -> combat-roll-math; (4) DerivedCalculator -> ranked-skills-engine -> skill-resolution-layer -> SkillState -> ActorEngine, and ActorEngine <-> missing-prereqs-tracker. The pivots are read-side modules (hardening, RageEngine, SkillState, missing-prereqs-tracker) that also contain write helpers importing ActorEngine statically. Runtime works because all bindings are used at call time, not module evaluation.
findings.intendedOwnership: Prepare-phase calculators depend only downward (infrastructure, data, ModifierEngine); the mutation gate depends on calculators, never the reverse.
findings.proposedSolution: Split read helpers from writers at the four pivots: move warnIfMixedTracks out of utils/hardening.js (or make hardening import ActorEngine lazily only in its restore helper); split RageEngine predicates (read) from rage start/end (write); split SkillState reads from its ActorEngine writes; have missing-prereqs-tracker receive ActorEngine by injection. Separately break ModifierEngine -> WeaponsEngine by having WeaponsEngine register weapon modifiers as a ModifierEngine source (inversion) rather than ModifierEngine importing it (global CR-05).
findings.alternatives: Accept cycles and add a census ratchet (A-P3) so no new edges join the SCC.
findings.regressionTests: Add a census check asserting the derived-calculator subgraph has no path to actor-engine.js; existing derived golden tests must stay green.
findings.simplificationBenefit: Derived calculators become testable without the mutation gate; one SCC shrinks.
findings.risk: Import-order regressions (TDZ) if a split module is evaluated before its dependency; verify with full CI.

findings.title: moveEmbeddedDocuments deletes from source before creating on target with no compensation
findings.observed: Source documents are deleted, then target create is attempted; a target failure (permission, validation) loses the item. The only caller, DropService, is orphan-unreferenced (registry), so the path is latent, not live.
findings.intendedOwnership: Cross-actor moves are create-then-delete or transactional (OSI atomicity for transfers).
findings.proposedSolution: Reorder to create on target, verify, then delete on source; or route through applyMutationPlan transactional on both actors. If DropService is confirmed dead, delete it (legacy C) and keep the fixed primitive.
findings.alternatives: Remove moveEmbeddedDocuments until a live caller needs it.
findings.regressionTests: Unit test: target create rejects -> source item still present.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Cross-actor drag between two owned actors with a non-GM user.
findings.simplificationBenefit: Removes a data-loss trap from the gate API.

findings.title: Five parallel plan-application entry points with different plan shapes
findings.observed: apply (createEmbedded/updateEmbedded/replaceSystem), applyDelta ({set,add,delete} features, 0 runtime callers), applyProgression (packet), executeEmbeddedPlan (plan-builders), applyMutationPlan ({create,set,update,add,delete}, transactional). A-15 names applyMutationPlan as the finalization commit, yet finalize-integration.js:56 uses applyProgression.
findings.intendedOwnership: One plan schema (applyMutationPlan) with adapters at the edges; A-15.
findings.proposedSolution: Declare applyMutationPlan canonical (C-ACT-3). Delete applyDelta (legacy C, no caller) after owner confirmation; express apply() adoption plans and applyProgression packets as builders that emit applyMutationPlan plans, keeping their validation.
findings.alternatives: Keep all five but document them in this contract as sanctioned.
findings.regressionTests: Parity tests for adoption (character-like-sheet.js:3282) and progression packet before/after rerouting.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Chargen, level-up and template adoption in Foundry.
findings.simplificationBenefit: One mutation-plan grammar; fewer execution paths.
findings.risk: Medium: progression finalization is a runtime-risk area.

findings.title: A-03 probe hits are sanctioned in-memory derived writers (path conflict only)
findings.observed: xp-engine.computeXpDerived writes system.derived.xp in memory and is called only from SWSEV2BaseActor._performDerivedCalculation (prepare phase). ActorEngine._applyDerivedUpdates folds DerivedCalculator output in memory and shares the derived-generation stamp. Neither persists derived data. xp-engine.js also contains applyXP (a writer via ActorEngine), so the module mixes calculator and mutation roles.
findings.intendedOwnership: Derived writers live under scripts/actors/** or are explicitly listed in A-03.
findings.proposedSolution: Move computeXpDerived to scripts/actors/derived/xp-derived.js (pure) and keep applyXP in progression; amend A-03 to name ActorEngine._applyDerivedUpdates as the sanctioned fold. Owner decides the A-03 wording.
findings.regressionTests: Existing XP display tests; add a test that computeXpDerived has no ActorEngine import.

findings.title: A-02/A-10 probe hits in actor-core: legitimate, false positive, or owner exception (character reset credits)
findings.observed: actor-utils.js:281/319 are the ActorEngine write primitive and its stale-reference retry (ActorEngine internals). actor-utils.js:397 is a JSDoc example (false positive). swse-actor-base.js:145 updates an unowned directory item and carries @mutation-exception. actor-sidebar-controls.js:125 is NPCTemplateImporter.create() (app factory, false positive). actor-sheet-base.js:1958 sets system.credits 0 inside _resetCharacterToBlank (user-confirmed destructive reset) via ActorEngine.updateActor, not via TransactionEngine; the sheet composes the reset payload itself (A-04). Exception candidate: a reset is not a transaction, but A-10 has no reset exception, so the owner must rule.
findings.proposedSolution: No code change for actor-utils/swse-actor-base/sidebar sites; add probe allow-list entries. Character reset: owner decides whether a blank-slate reset is an A-10 exception; if yes, move the reset payload into an ActorEngine/progression reset service and comment it.

findings.title: Condition-track penalty table duplicated in four modules
findings.observed: Identical literal [0,-1,-2,-5,-10,0] in four places; defense-calculator prefers derived.damage.conditionPenalty and falls back to its own copy. Values agree today.
findings.intendedOwnership: One condition-track rule owner (combat ConditionTrackRules) consumed by actor-core.
findings.proposedSolution: Expose the table from ConditionTrackRules (or a pure constants module) and import it at the four sites. No value changes.
findings.regressionTests: Golden defense lifecycle test plus a unit test asserting all consumers read one table.

findings.title: ActorEngine monkey-patches actor.items (filter/some/map/find) on every update, unconditionally
findings.observed: Labelled DEV MODE but not gated: the first updateActor/updateEmbeddedDocuments on an actor replaces four collection methods with wrappers that call SentinelEngine.reportSSOTViolation. With sentinelMode OFF (default) each call returns early; with DEV/STRICT every items.filter (including DerivedCalculator internals) captures a stack trace. This is a runtime monkey-patch (A-09) owned by actor-core.
findings.proposedSolution: Gate instrumentation on SentinelEngine.isEnabled() (or remove it; the census now measures SSOT statically).
findings.regressionTests: Test: with Sentinel OFF, actor.items.filter is the native method after updateActor.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Profile a large actor sheet with Sentinel DEV.

findings.title: Deprecated write wrappers in actor-utils.js and a second safeActorUpdate
findings.observed: batchActorUpdates and safeActorUpdate (actor-utils) are marked DEPRECATED and have no importers; they call the raw primitive applyActorUpdateAtomic directly, bypassing ActorEngine validation. runtime-safety.js has a different safeActorUpdate routed via ActorEngine but the module is unreachable (importer hardening-init.js only).
findings.proposedSolution: Delete batchActorUpdates/safeActorUpdate from actor-utils (legacy C) and move applyActorUpdateAtomic into scripts/governance/actor-engine/ (non-exported outside the gate).
findings.regressionTests: Static test: applyActorUpdateAtomic imported only by actor-engine.js.

findings.title: Dual flag scope: setFlag("swse") is remapped to "foundryvtt-swse" while most reads use flags.swse
findings.observed: SWSEActorBase.setFlag/unsetFlag rewrite scope "swse" to the system id; getFlag("swse") reads foundryvtt-swse then falls back to flags.swse. Code that writes via actor.update({"flags.swse.x"}) persists to flags.swse, while ActorEngine.updateActorFlags(actor,"swse",...) persists to flags["foundryvtt-swse"]. git grep counts ~1,535 flags.swse references vs ~182 flags["foundryvtt-swse"]. Direct property reads of flags.swse.x miss values written through setFlag("swse"). Not traced per key.
findings.intendedOwnership: One canonical flag namespace with one accessor.
findings.proposedSolution: Inventory keys written through each path (census of setFlag scope + flags.swse writes) and pick one namespace; until then, require ActorEngine flag helpers and getFlag for reads. Owner decision on the canonical scope.
findings.regressionTests: Per-key round-trip tests write via each path and read via each accessor.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Verify setFlag("swse") persistence location in Foundry v13.
findings.risk: Migration of persisted flags is a runtime-risk area.

findings.title: regainForcePoints writes untyped system.forcePoints.value, bypassing the typed Force Point ledger
findings.observed: spendForcePoint routes through ActorEngine.spendForcePoints receipts ("Force V2: no untyped balance write"), but regainForcePoints writes the balance directly through updateActor. Its only caller is the GM workspace refresh action. ActorEngine.gainForcePoints exists (actor-engine.js:2077).
findings.intendedOwnership: Force Point gains go through ForcePointsService / ActorEngine.gainForcePoints.
findings.proposedSolution: Reroute regainForcePoints to ActorEngine.gainForcePoints (or a ForcePointsService refresh). Whether a full refresh should be ledgered is not a rules question; the restore-to-max semantics stay unchanged.
findings.regressionTests: Test GM refresh produces a ledger entry and same final value.
findings.foundryAcceptance: GM refresh on a live actor.

findings.title: Passive ability re-registration runs 2-3 times per mutation
findings.observed: AbilityExecutionCoordinator.registerActorAbilities runs in every prepareDerivedData, and again in updateActor (every client, every update), createItem and deleteItem hooks. Foundry re-prepares after each of these events, so the hook calls appear redundant. Hypothesis: not measured.
findings.proposedSolution: Instrument with ActorPerfDiagnostics counters; if confirmed, remove the three hook registrations (keep prepare-phase registration).
findings.regressionTests: Counter-based test: one registration per update.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Measure with performanceDiagnostics on a large actor.
findings.risk: Medium: ordering assumptions about passive modifiers before derived.

findings.title: Unreachable actor-core modules
findings.observed: Four orphans with no static, dynamic, template or pack references to their symbols (git grep); hp-recompute-hooks.js is imported only by orphan governance-integration.js and a test.
findings.intendedOwnership: No dead modules in runtime tree.
findings.proposedSolution: Delete the four orphans (legacy C). hp-recompute-hooks: owner decides wire vs delete (U-ACT-01).

findings.title: actor-engine.js (4,890 lines) mixes the mutation gate, resource ledgers, canonical-shape normalizers and plan engines
findings.observed: One object literal holds: gate methods, Force/Destiny ledgers with queues and outboxes, damage/condition/second-wind orchestration, five plan grammars, recovery snapshots, and ~500 lines of canonical-shape normalization. docs/audits/actor-engine-extraction-plan.md already proposes a thin-facade extraction.
findings.intendedOwnership: ActorEngine as a facade over internal modules in scripts/governance/actor-engine/.
findings.proposedSolution: Extract internal seams (not new authorities): ledger module (FP/Destiny), plan executor (applyMutationPlan + rollback), shape normalizer (moves to governance/mutation/mutation-normalization-service.js which already exists). Keep the ActorEngine public API unchanged.
findings.regressionTests: Existing 353 CI tests that import ActorEngine.
findings.simplificationBenefit: Smaller review surface for the most-imported module.

findings.title: DerivedCalculator.computeAll is monkey-patched at init by the force domain (Skill Focus non-stacking post-filter)
findings.observed: registerForceSuiteRuntimeRepairs (called first in init, index.js:102) replaces DerivedCalculator.computeAll with a wrapper that calls the original and then rewrites the returned updates via suppressDuplicateSkillFocusInUpdates. The canonical derived calculator therefore does not produce the final skill totals by itself; a stacking rule lives in a force-domain patch module, and the wrapper mutates the object returned from the signature cache.
findings.intendedOwnership: Skill/stacking behaviour inside DerivedCalculator/ModifierEngine (A-09 clean cutover; A-01).
findings.proposedSolution: Fold the Skill Focus non-stacking logic into the skill-total computation that DerivedCalculator already calls (or into ModifierEngine stacking for the Skill Focus source), with its existing tests, then delete the wrapper. No change to the stacking result itself; if the intended stacking behaviour is not documented, record it before moving (CLAUDE.md §3).
findings.regressionTests: Golden skill totals with duplicate Skill Focus sources before/after folding; assert DerivedCalculator.computeAll is not reassigned after init.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Character with Skill Focus from two sources, sheet totals.
findings.simplificationBenefit: Removes a live patch over the core derived pipeline.
findings.risk: Medium: skill totals are visible everywhere.
